provenance.source: Income Tax Rates Act 1986; Medicare Levy Act 1986; PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Australia; ATO rates for 2026-27
provenance.notes: The 2026-27 rates were confirmed against PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries on 31 August 2026, including the reduction of the lowest rate from 16% to 15% from 1 July 2026. The Medicare levy low-income threshold and the LITO taper come from secondary sources and are not verified against the ATO.

verificationTodo: Confirm the Medicare levy singles threshold of AUD 28,011 and the shade-in ceiling of AUD 35,014 for 2026-27 against the ATO.
Confirm the low income tax offset of AUD 700 and its two taper rates for 2026-27.
Family Medicare levy thresholds are not modelled at all; a taxpayer with a spouse or dependants may pay less than shown.
omissions: HELP, VET and other study loan repayments are not modelled, and they materially change take-home pay for many graduates.
The Medicare levy surcharge for high earners without private hospital cover is not modelled.
Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by the employer on top of salary and are not a deduction from your pay, so they do not appear here.
Family and seniors Medicare levy thresholds, and the seniors and pensioners tax offset, are not modelled.

scale.note: The lowest rate falls from 16% to 15% from 1 July 2026 and to 14% from 1 July 2027 under the legislated tax cuts.

medicareLevy.note: No levy at all below the threshold. Between the threshold and the ceiling only 10 cents in the dollar of the excess is charged, which is a shade-in, not a bracket. Above the ceiling the full 2% applies to the whole taxable income.

lowIncomeTaxOffset.note: A non-refundable offset against tax. It cannot create a refund of its own, and it is withdrawn at two different rates, which lifts the effective marginal rate between AUD 37,500 and AUD 66,667.

regions.name: Australia
regions.note: Australian income tax is federal only. States raise payroll tax from employers, not income tax from individuals.

inputSchema.label: Gross salary (per month)
inputSchema.help: Gross pay before tax, month by month. Do not include employer superannuation: it is paid on top of your salary, not out of it.

inputSchema.label: PAYG tax withheld (per month)
inputSchema.help: Tax withheld by your employer, used to show whether you are due a refund.

inputSchema.label: Work-related deductions
inputSchema.help: Car, travel, clothing, self-education, tools and home office costs incurred earning your income, that your employer did not reimburse. You need records for anything above AUD 300 in total.

inputSchema.label: Gifts to deductible gift recipients
inputSchema.help: Donations of AUD 2 or more to an organisation with DGR status. A donation cannot create or increase a tax loss.

inputSchema.label: Personal deductible super contributions
inputSchema.help: Voluntary contributions you make from after-tax money and then claim a deduction for, within the concessional cap. Do not include your employer's compulsory contributions.
